question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 24 minutes, respectively, and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 15 minutes. The capacity of the tank is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Work** (LCM of 20, 24, 15) = 120 units.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 6, **Pipe B** = 5, and **(A + B + C)** = 8.

Efficiency of **Emptying Pipe C** = 8 − (6 + 5) = −3 units/min.

Since 3 units/min corresponds to 3 gallons/min, 1 unit = 1 gallon.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 gallons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of **filling pipes** (A + B) = 6 + 5 = 11 units/min.

⇒ Efficiency of **waste pipe C** = (A + B + C) − (A + B) = 8 − 11 = −3 units/min.

⇒ Negative sign indicates **emptying**.

⇒ Time taken by **Pipe C** to empty the tank = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 minutes.

⇒ **Capacity of tank** = Rate of emptying × Time taken = 3 gallons/min × 40 min = 120 gallons.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 gallons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Efficiency of a filling pipe is taken as **positive**, while the efficiency of an emptying pipe is taken as **negative**.

Capacity Formula

The **total capacity** of a tank is calculated as the **Rate of flow** × **Time** taken to fill or empty the tank.

LCM Method

Total Work is assumed as the **Least Common Multiple** of individual time periods to simplify efficiency calculations.</p
